notes: Priority: low-latency driver assistant + reranking for routing. Heavy constraint: must support VPC/private deployment and KMS; data residency in NA required. Team: Head of Platform (R. Gupta), ML infra lead (S. Alvarez). AE notes: 'very cost-aware but will pay for predictable latency' — emphasis on determinism over raw throughput. Current ask: define p50/p95/p99 for both streaming (chunked token streams to clients) and non-streaming (single-response) flows and agree on where to measure (client-side vs server ingest). They observed differences of ~120-350ms when client-side timers used; want gating SLOs by route.
latency_slo_alignment: Oxbow requirement: separate SLOs for streaming vs non-streaming endpoints.
Proposed SLOs: non-streaming p50<60ms, p95<220ms, p99<500ms for control-plane routes (inference only).
Proposed SLOs: streaming p50<40ms (first-byte), p95<180ms (steady-state per-chunk), p99<450ms (client-observed chunk delays).
Measurement alignment: agree to capture server-side ingest timestamp + server-response-first-byte; client will also send SDK-labeled send/receive timestamps for correlation.
Instrumentation plan: use request-id propagated end-to-end; provide sample instrumentation lib for iOS/Android/Node to normalize clock skew with NTP offset sampling.

Definition note: p50/p95/p99 computed on server-side processing latency first, then validated against client-observed distribution. Final contract will use server-side SLOs with a client-side tolerance buffer (+/- 30-50ms) documented in SLA.
Edge cases: streaming cancellation, long-poll fallbacks — will treat canceled streams as non-violations unless final chunk latency exceeds thresholds.
throughput_and_capacity_requirements: Target steady-state throughput: 2,500 concurrent chats across regions (NA primary) with peak bursts up to 5k qps for light embed/rerank ops.
Reserved GPU planning: initial reservation for 8x A100-class GPUs (or equivalent) with autoscale policy for burst to 12 GPUs for vendor-verified quantized model variant.
Throughput SLA ask: 99.9% request acceptance at provisioned throughput; fallback to lower-cost model variant acceptable for non-critical traffic.
sla_negotiation_points: SLO measurement source (server vs client) — legal wants server-side canonical metric; infra prefers combined telemetry for incident triage.
Availability SLA: 99.95% monthly uptime desired for Dedicated control plane; Oxbow requests credit tiers and runbook access.
Penalty/credit structure: Oxbow will push for transparently measured p95 credits tied to customer impact windows.
Data residency & auditability: require exportable audit logs for inference calls and KMS key use logs.
use_case_summary: Deploy Redwood Dedicated inside VPC for real-time driver assistant (streaming chat) and a rerank pipeline for ETA predictions (non-streaming). Must guarantee predictable latency for driver app (mobile) and batch rerank throughput for nightly optimizations.
